title: Prime Factors
problem: Given an integer N (2 <= N <= 1000000000) on a single line of input, print its prime factors from smallest to largest, separated by spaces, repeating a factor as many times as it divides N. For example, 12 = 2 x 2 x 3, so the answer is 2 2 3. A prime number is its own only factor.
starter_code:
# Read an integer N.
# Print its prime factors in increasing order, separated by spaces,
# e.g. 12 -> 2 2 3.

# Write your code here

hints.1: Try dividing by the smallest possible factor first, and keep dividing by it for as long as it goes in.
hints.2: Start d at 2. While d * d <= N: if N % d == 0, record d and set N = N // d (staying on the same d); otherwise move d up by one. When the loop ends, if N is still above 1, it is a prime factor too. Stopping at the square root keeps it fast even for the biggest N.

failure_explanation: Divide out each factor as many times as it goes in, so repeated factors are all printed, smallest first. Only try divisors while d * d <= N, which keeps large inputs fast enough, and remember that whatever is left above 1 after the loop is a prime factor too. Use whole-number division (//), not /.
